9 Best Things to Do in Marrakesh 🕌✨ 1) Stay in a Riad 🛏️  feel the authentic Moroccan vibe, from the mosaic tiles to the whisper-quiet courtyards. Riads offer privacy, fewer crowds, and a home-away-from-home feel with traditional decor, often a peaceful rooftop terrace, and staff who treat you like family. Perfect for a truly Moroccan experience without the hotel hustle. 2) Best Coffee at Bacha Coffee ☕️✨ (Location: https://goo.gl/maps/6u3Xx9J9xqv1w9Qw7) Silky espresso, perfectly balanced blends, and a chic, relaxed atmosphere. Great latte art, friendly baristas, and a bright, stylish space to post your vibes. Pro tip: try their signature crush coffee and pastry pairing. 3) Explore the Souks 🧿🌀 Fun tip: haggle with a smile, never agree to the first price! Make it a playful game, sample spices, and test your bargaining skills. Lose yourself in ribbons of color, leather, pottery, and lamps. The thrill of the find is half the fun! 4) Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa 🕌 A jaw-dropping historic site with intricate tilework, carved wood, and serene courtyards. It’s a perfect spot for photos that scream old-world Marrakech charm. 5) Jardin Majorelle 🌿💙 iconic cobalt-blue paths, lush botanical displays, and a peaceful escape from the market buzz. A must-see for color lovers and plant enthusiasts, plus it’s connected to the Yves Saint Laurent legacy. 6) Ourika Valley Day Trip 🚙🌄 about 1 hour from central Marrakech (depending on traffic). What to expect: stunning valley scenery, Berber villages, waterfalls, and a cooler climate. A refreshing break from the medina with photo-worthy viewpoints. 7) Agafay Desert Experience 🐫🏜️ Highlights: camel ride under the open sky, squad  bike moments, and magical desert views. Luxe touch: stay at a desert camp with plush lounges, gourmet meals, and starlit dinners. Perfect for a memorable  outing. 8) Dinner at La Trattoria 🍝🇮🇹  warm, cozy ambiance with authentic Italian flavors in Marrakech. Great for a relaxed evening, fresh pastas, and a lively dining vibe after a day of exploration. 9) Jemaa el-Fnaa - The Heart of Marrakech 🎭💃 Do it for the vibes: bustling square, street performances, snake charmers, and a feast for the senses. Pro tip: bring some cash for photos with performers and for quick bites. Best times: late afternoon into evening when the energy peaks. #Marrakesh #Morocco #TravelTikTok #Riads #Souks

😍Morocco like Pinterest: the most beautiful hotels  🇲🇦  📍 Royal Mansour Marrakech One of the most luxurious hotels in the world, where every guest stays in a private riad with its own courtyard and pool. Carved ceilings, mosaics, and palm gardens. Breakfasts on the terrace and a spa under a glass dome. 📍 El Fenn A place where Morocco meets contemporary art. Bright walls, terracotta rooftop pools, vintage furniture, and rich colors. A bohemian vibe with sunsets overlooking the medina. 📍 La Mamounia A true Marrakech legend. Expansive gardens, arched galleries, emerald tiles, and a pool you’ll want to spend all day in. Classic luxury with history. 📍 Riad Yasmine The iconic Instagram riad with an emerald pool and pink walls. Small, cozy, and incredibly photogenic. Breakfast by the pool with flower petals. 📍 Amanjena Minimalism with Moroccan architecture. Sandy tones, reflective pools, and perfect symmetry. 📍 Kasbah Tamadot A hotel in the Atlas Mountains with views over the valleys. Terraces, Berber style, and warm sunset light. 📍 The Oberoi Marrakech Modern luxury with an oriental touch. Grand pools, arches, reflective water, and clean geometry. 📍 Scarabeo Camp White tents in the Agafay desert. Minimalism, sand dunes, camels, and caramel-colored sunsets. #moroccotravel #luxuryhotels #riadlife #travelinspo #bucketlist

#hassan2 #saharaofmorocco🇲🇦 #maroc #pourtoiii #morocco  🇲🇦 Nasser Bourita à l’ONU : les grandes lignes du discours du Maroc À l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, le ministre marocain des Affaires étrangères a présenté les principales priorités du Royaume face aux défis internationaux. 🌍 Un monde en pleine mutation Le Maroc appelle à défendre le multilatéralisme, le droit international et la coopération internationale dans un contexte marqué par la multiplication des crises et des conflits. 🛡️ Lutte contre les groupes armés Rabat insiste sur la nécessité de lutter contre les groupes armés non étatiques, le terrorisme et les réseaux criminels, ainsi que contre les États qui les financent ou les soutiennent. 🌱 Climat et sécurité de l’eau Le Maroc rappelle son engagement contre le changement climatique et met en avant sa politique de barrages, dessalement, réutilisation des eaux usées et gestion des ressources hydriques. 🇵🇸 Palestine et Jérusalem Le Royaume réaffirme son soutien à la création d’un État palestinien indépendant et souverain, dans les frontières de 1967, avec Jérusalem-Est comme capitale. Il appelle également au cessez-le-feu, à l’acheminement de l’aide humanitaire à Gaza et au soutien de l’Autorité palestinienne. 🌍 L’Afrique au cœur de la diplomatie marocaine Le Maroc défend une Afrique actrice de son propre destin : infrastructures, sécurité alimentaire, énergie, formation, santé, eau et développement économique sont au cœur de ses partenariats avec le continent. 🇲🇦 Sahara marocain : six principes réaffirmés Bourita affirme que le règlement doit passer par le processus politique de l’ONU et que l’initiative d’autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine constitue, selon le Maroc, le cadre de règlement proposé. Il rejette le statu quo et appelle à une solution politique définitive. 🤝 Le Maroc candidat au Conseil de sécurité Enfin, le Royaume confirme sa candidature à un siège de membre non permanent du Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU pour le mandat 2028-2029, en mettant en avant son engagement en faveur de la paix, du développement, du droit international et du multilatéralisme. 🇲🇦 Un discours centré sur trois mots : paix, souveraineté et coopération.

Would you wander Marrakech alone?  One thing I was honestly nervous about before coming to Marrakech for the first time was safety, especially as a woman travelling alone. Social media can make the medina look super intimidating, chaotic, and overwhelming, but my experience has actually been really positive. Of course you need to stay aware like in any big city, but I’ve spent hours wandering the souks, getting lost in little alleyways, shopping, stopping for mint tea, and exploring on my own and I genuinely felt okay. One thing that helped SO much this time was not carrying all my luggage around with me 😅 dragging a huge backpack through crowded streets instantly makes you feel more stressed and overwhelmed. I used @bounce luggage storage so I could explore Marrakech freely for the day before my riad check-in, and it made such a difference. I could actually enjoy the medina instead of worrying about my bags the entire time. Bounce has thousands of locations worldwide and is a super reliable resource if you find yourself in a similar situation as me. If you’re travelling soon, you can use my code SARAHBOUNCE for a discount! #travelhacks #travelreccommendations #solotraveller

If you’re only staying in Marrakesh, you’re missing half of Morocco. We booked a 3-day Imperial Cities tour and honestly, it changed the whole trip. Day one started in Casablanca at the Hassan II Mosque! one of the largest mosques in the world and the only one in Morocco open to non-Muslims. What makes it even more special? Every Moroccan citizen contributed just $2 toward building it. It sits right on the Atlantic Ocean and the architecture is genuinely breathtaking. From there we drove to Rabat, Morocco’s capital city, which most tourists completely skip. We walked through the Portuguese and Jewish historic neighbourhoods, visited the beaches and soaked in centuries of history. Our guide arranged everything! we even had free time to explore and shop. We ended the day arriving in Fez, checked into our Riad and sat down for dinner. Accommodation, breakfast and dinner all pre-arranged. Genuinely stress free. Day two was a full five-hour guided tour through the Fez Medina, the oldest medieval city in the world, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with over 9,000 streets. We visited a traditional tannery where leather has been dyed the same way for over 1,000 years, met master craftsmen and had the chance to commission custom furniture, carpets and ceramics. Moroccan craftsmanship is on another level. We also visited al-Qarawiyyin — the first university ever founded in the world, built in 859 CE by Fatima al-Fihri, a Muslim woman who used her inheritance to create something that has outlasted empires. We ended in Chefchaouen — the famous blue city nestled in the Rif Mountains. Dinner at the Riad, breakfast arranged in the morning, and then the whole day was ours to explore freely. No guide, just a curated list of must-see spots and good vibes. Marrakesh is beautiful. But Morocco is so much more than one city. @GetYourGuide #MoroccoTravel #MoroccoItinerary #MoroccoTravelGuide #VisitMorocco #ImperialCitiesMorocco​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
